clue.text: Treasury issues insurance payments to cover 007

indicators.note: to cover means the first piece wraps around the second, holding it inside

parts.note: premiums are the regular payments made for an insurance policy
007 is the code number of James Bond, the fictional spy

explanation.surface: The Treasury puts out money from insurance premiums to fund a spy's mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' wraps the insurance word around the spy. In Britain these are government savings bonds whose interest is paid as prizes in a monthly draw.
explanation.definitionFit: These prize-paying savings certificates are issued by the Treasury through National Savings, so they are literally its issues.

clue.text: Describe what might be needed in close-run election

definitions.meaning: to describe events is to tell or narrate them in order

definitions.text: what might be needed in close-run election
definitions.meaning: when a vote is very tight the ballots are counted a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to tell it over; a second tally of votes is a fresh count.

clue.text: Some link wild animal's fur with spy's family

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, plus the possessive S
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A spy's relatives are connected to a pelt from a wild creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held opens with 'Some link', which plays no clear part and may be an OCR misreading.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of the mole, a small burrowing creature, with its velvety pelt, is what the word first named.

clue.text: Cause downfall of a French party

parts.note: un is the French for a (masculine)
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A French party brings about someone's ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin or bring someone down is the sense of this verb, as in 'pride was his ruin'.

clue.text: Chess player has to protect such a scoundrel

parts.note: in chess one side is called Black, the other White
to guard is to protect

explanation.surface: A chess player is told to defend a villain on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' and 'such a' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a villain or rogue who behaves dishonourably.

clue.text: Not in any way stated as experience

indicators.note: stated means the word for experience is spoken, and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: know-how is practical experience or skill

explanation.surface: Someone says they have no experience at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect or informal adverb meaning by no means, in no manner whatever.

clue.text: A leak? Refer to attendant

parts.note: see, as in 'see page 4', tells a reader to refer to something
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: Someone spots a leak and tells the attendant to deal with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly escaping through a crack is a slow leak.

clue.text: Military "bull": suggestions to be taken up with finesse

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: tips are helpful suggestions
and means together with
polish means refinement or finesse

explanation.surface: Army bullshit: suggestions are to be adopted with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken up' turns TIPS into SPIT. 'Bull' is British forces' slang for excessive cleaning and smartness for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive attention to cleaning boots and kit, demanded on parade, is what soldiers call bull.

clue.text: Top man has finished with scoundrels completely

parts.note: the head is the top of the body, and head means top man or chief
over means ended or finished
heels are cads or scoundrels

explanation.surface: The boss has done with his rogues once and for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' reads as one idea, but only 'Top' gives HEAD, with 'man' part of that phrase; 'has' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, usually of falling in love, means utterly or totally.

clue.text: Drunk chose to hold lamppost initially

indicators.note: to hold means the first word contains the second piece

parts.note: picked means chose

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word lamppost

explanation.surface: A drunk chose to cling to a lamppost.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Amateur let the wrong competitor on the track

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An amateur allowed the wrong runner onto the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner or other sporting competitor in track and field events.

clue.text: Not completely accurate- South twice added personal support

indicators.note: not completely means the word for accurate loses its last letter

parts.note: true means accurate

indicators.note: twice means the abbreviation is written two times

explanation.surface: A slightly inaccurate report says the south has twice added a personal support.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded belt worn to support a hernia is a support for the wearer's body.

clue.text: Spotted horse in southern botanic gardens with no hair

parts.note: Kew Gardens in west London are the Royal Botanic Gardens
bald means having no hair

explanation.surface: A dappled horse in a southern garden has lost its mane.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with irregular patches of white and another colour, not black, is described this way.

clue.text: Lily from S. Africa put pan on stove this way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits below it, so the pan follows the stove

parts.note: an Aga is a make of heavy cooking range
taken as written
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: Put the pan on the stove like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link word. An AGA is a large cast-iron range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: The African lily, a blue-flowered plant native to southern Africa, has this botanical name.

clue.text: Only zero, however

parts.note: nothing is zero, nil
but means however

explanation.surface: Just zero, though.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means merely or solely, as in 'he wants only the best'.

clue.text: It comes under various headings including "engine fuel"

indicators.note: the phrase says the words before it hold the answer, as a heading includes what falls under it

explanation.surface: A clerk files an item under several headings, one of them engine fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'under' and 'various'; 'It comes' is a link. DERV is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: British term for diesel oil used to power road vehicles, from the initials of diesel-engined road vehicle.

clue.text: N.E. European one isn't a reformation

indicators.note: a reformation forms the letters again in a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from north-east Europe is no fan of the Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformation' rearranges ONEISNTA, with the A from 'a' included.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Baltic state at the north-east edge of Europe, across the gulf from Finland.

clue.text: Old Venetian sport

definitions.meaning: Marco, the medieval explorer from Venice who travelled to China
a team game played on horseback with mallets

explanation.definitionFit: Marco the Venetian traveller shares his surname with the horseback stick-and-ball game.

clue.text: School using mounted warriors weapon

definitions.meaning: ... College is an English independent school in West Sussex
a lance was the spear carried by knights on horseback, so using it is the verb form

explanation.definitionFit: A Sussex public school shares its name with wielding the long spear of a cavalryman.

clue.text: Physical activity gear left in ship by don

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
port is the left side of a ship
to don clothing is to wear it

explanation.surface: Gym kit was left aboard ship by a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; 'don' looks like a university lecturer but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn for sport or exercise.

clue.text: Building Cresta Run will be postponed if ice covers it

indicators.note: covers it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The famous toboggan run's fixture will be delayed if it ices over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is an ice toboggan course in St Moritz, Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposing structure is a large building.

clue.text: Want help with ordinary writing?

parts.note: to long for something is to want it
a hand is help, as in 'give me a hand'

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you need help with your handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing by hand in full words, as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Male accepts welcome lift: its almost bliss

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
ave is a Latin greeting, a hail or welcome

explanation.surface: A man takes a welcome lift, and it is nearly paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' is a link; 'its almost bliss' adds a second hint: heaven, a word for bliss, without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or hoist with effort is the verb's sense.

clue.text: First of orang-utans to survive on fruit

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word orang-utans

parts.note: to live is to survive

explanation.surface: The first orang-utans survive by eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oval stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree, eaten or pressed for oil.

clue.text: Shoot to stop

definitions.meaning: a stalk or shoot of a plant
to staunch or stop a flow, as of blood

explanation.definitionFit: A plant stalk shares its spelling with the verb to stanch a flow.

clue.text: Chips with an unusual vegetable

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unusual order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Chips served with an odd green vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CHIPSAN; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy green plant eaten cooked or raw, Popeye's favourite.

clue.text: Hearing about four or six of little importance

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second piece

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
VI is six in Roman numerals; IV, four, works as well, placed after TR

explanation.surface: A court hearing over four or six minor matters is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: Either numeral fits: TR+IV+IAL and TRI+VI+AL both spell the answer, hence 'four or six'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty or insignificant matters are of small importance.

clue.text: Mechanics bribe — a thousand in cash

parts.note: to grease someone's palm is to bribe them, so grease is a bribe

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: money is cash
K is short for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: Mechanics are paid a bribe of a thousand in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural in the clue as held, but the answer is one mechanic; the clue probably read Mechanic's, with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a mechanic who works on engines and gets oily.
